# Open Telestrator

> Free, open-source sports telestrator and live commentary studio. Draw over any sport as it happens, commentate, and send viewers one link — in a browser, on a desktop or a phone, with no account, no capture card and nothing to download.

Open Telestrator is a static web app (React, WebRTC and PeerJS) hosted on GitHub Pages. The host shares a browser tab or a camera as the video source, draws over it with arrows, circles and freehand strokes, records instant replays, mixes commentary audio, and broadcasts the program to viewers peer-to-peer. Viewers — and phones acting as extra camera angles — join by opening a link or scanning a QR code, and the player can be embedded in another site with a plain iframe.

There is nothing to install: the site is the studio, and it can be added to a home screen as a PWA. The same page adapts to whatever it is on — a mouse-driven window keeps a rail of controls down the side, and anything held in a hand gets a bar along the bottom with the panel as a sheet, controls at least 44px on their short side and palm rejection on the drawing canvas.

The program can also be sent out to a live platform over WebRTC, using WHIP (WebRTC-HTTP Ingestion Protocol). No encoder, extension or companion process is involved: the browser posts one SDP offer and publishes the composited picture. Three services are built in — Restream (which forwards to YouTube, Twitch, Facebook and around thirty more, and accepts WHIP on its free plan), Cloudflare Stream (hosts the feed and plays it back over WHEP, forwarding nowhere) and LiveKit (an account or deployment of your own, able to push out over RTMP from an egress). A platform's own ingest address speaks RTMP, which a browser cannot open a socket for, which is why the stream goes through a service.

- Home page: https://spuds0588.github.io/open-telestrator/
- Studio app: https://spuds0588.github.io/open-telestrator/app.html
- Source code and MIT licence: https://github.com/Spuds0588/open-telestrator

## Key facts

- Cost: free and open source (MIT); no account, subscription or paid tier.
- Equipment: any webcam, phone camera or browser tab; no capture card or mixer needed.
- Sports: any — the video source is whatever plays in a browser tab or comes from a camera.
- Broadcast: live-only, peer-to-peer over WebRTC. Viewers form a relay tree, so the stream never passes through a server and the host's uplink stays small.
- Stream out: over WHIP to Restream, Cloudflare Stream or LiveKit; nothing to install, since the browser is the encoder.
- Viewing: any modern browser, phone or desktop, with play/pause, volume, full screen and picture-in-picture; share by link or embed in an iframe.
- Studio entries: the landing page lives at `/`; the host studio, `?watch=` viewer and `?camera=` cameraman entries live at `/app.html`.
- Installing it: optional. The page works as it is, and a PWA install from the browser menu adds it to the home screen or dock.
- Limits: RTSP and RTMP cannot play in a browser at all, so those links are refused as inputs; screen/tab capture needs `getDisplayMedia`, which iOS Safari does not have.
